You're not looking at the big picture. YES, Voat has a limited form of censorship (and one I think should be relaxed), however, people come here because it has censorship. Let me repeat that: People come here FOR the censorship. As long as there are alternative websites to go to that are completely uncensored (as well as ones censored in different ways), then this website is actually providing a service by censoring unwanted content. Some less unsavory terms for censorship include curation and moderation. For a site the size of Voat, which is not shaping public opinion or holding undue influence on public discourse, censorship is not necessarily bad. It's when you get to sites the size of facebook, twitter, or reddit, that censorship moves beyond community desire for expression and into suppression. It's the difference between not being welcome in a bar, vs not being welcome in the whole damn city.

Censorship on Voat provides several valuable services. It hides Indian spam. It hides streaming video spam. It hides big dick pill spam. It hides Amalek spam (HINT FUCKING HINT). It highlights good content. And think on that for a second, mein neger. When something gets upvoted, everything else gets comparatively moved down just a teeny bit and therefore is less likely to be seen. Every time good content is upvoted, everything else, even other good content, is being just a tiny bit censored, and those tiny bits add up unless countered with upvotes for that other content too. This is how community moderation works. It's not a perfect system, it can be gamed, but people come here because in general, the censorship provides more positives for them than negatives.

If you want a complete freedom from censorship, you can make your own site, and hopefully host it on TOR for when the CP shows up.

As for the account restrictions, I agree that downvotes aren't a perfect way to decide that, but then again, neither are bans from moderators (just see that lackwit @HenryCorp).
